ⓐ _____ she could enter high school. After graduating from high school in 1932, she was admitted to a black college at the age of fifteen. Her mentor gladly offered special classes just for her, but he was not happy when he had to tell his outstanding student about her career opportunities. “You would make a good research mathematician,” he told his seventeen-year-old student, “and I’m going to prepare you for this career.” Katherine asked, “ⓒ _____ will I find a job?” “That,” he replied, “will be your problem.” The path ahead was unclear and full of obstacles, but Katherine knew ⓓ _____ she had the strength to make her own way. In 1935, at the age of eighteen, Katherine graduated from college with highest honors and began her career as a teacher at a black public school. At ⓔ _____ time, teaching was the only option available to her.

answer: (A) It is because her hometown had a segregated education system, and black students could not enter high school. Inclusive Language Language has the power to shape our attitudes and behaviors. Inclusive language serves as an important tool for acknowledging diversity, encouraging sensitivity to differences, and promoting equal opportunities.
(A) It actively contributes to breaking biases and discriminatory language and to building a welcoming environment of inclusivity. For example, adopting the gender-neutral term “mail carrier” instead of “mailman” or “mailwoman” conveys a powerful message: it recognizes the capabilities of individuals of either gender for delivering the mail. (B) This seemingly minor change reflects a more extensive commitment to acknowledging the ability of every person, regardless of his or her gender.
(C) Many ancient languages disappeared because younger generations stopped using them. Another aspect of inclusive communication, known as person-first language, encourages us to prioritize the individual over any defining characteristic. Instead of saying “colored people,” we should use “people of color.” Similarly, opting for “person with blindness” over “blind person” highlights the unique identity and dignity of each individual while avoiding the reduction of a person to an unusual characteristic.
(D) In summary, inclusive language plays a crucial role in creating a fair and welcoming society, where every individual can embrace his or her genuine self without the fear of exclusion. (E) Such language choices can positively influence the way people understand and respect one another.

다음 글을 읽고, inclusive communication의 또 다른 측면으로 언급된 표현을 본문에서 찾아 두 단어 이내로 쓰시오.
→ _____ 1회차 실전 모의고사

So her father moved the family 200 kilometers away so that she could enter high school. After graduating from high school in 1932, she was admitted to a black college at the age of fifteen. Katherine asked, "Where will I find a job?" ⓐ"That," he replied, "will be your problem." The path ahead was unclear and full of obstacles, but Katherine knew she had the strength to make her own way. In 1935, at the age of eighteen, Katherine graduated from college with highest honors and began her career as a teacher at a black public school. At that time, teaching was the only option available to her. 실전 모의고사 2회차

body:
다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.
Katherine Johnson was born on August 26, 1918, in West Virginia, in the U.S., and was the youngest of four children in a black family. Katherine was a math prodigy from early childhood. Reflecting on her youth, Katherine once said, "I counted everything─the steps to the road, the steps up to church, the number of dishes, spoons, and forks I washed." She excitedly added, "I couldn't wait to get to high school to take algebra and geometry." But Katherine's hometown had a segregated education system, and black students could not enter high school. So her father moved the family 200 kilometers away so that she could enter high school. After graduating from high school in 1932, she was admitted to a black college at the age of fifteen. By her junior year, she had taken all the math courses the college could offer. Her mentor gladly offered special classes just for her, but he was not happy when he had to tell his outstanding student about her career opportunities. "You would make a good research mathematician," he told his seventeen-year-old student, "and I'm going to prepare you for this career." Katherine asked, "Where will I find a job?" ⓐ"That," he replied, "will be your problem." The path ahead was unclear and full of obstacles, but Katherine knew she had the strength to make her own way. In 1935, at the age of eighteen, Katherine graduated from college with highest honors and began her career as a teacher at a black public school. At that time, teaching was the only option available to her. 실전 모의고사 2회차

It actively contributes to breaking biases and discriminatory language and to building a welcoming environment of inclusivity. For example, adopting the gender-neutral term “mail carrier” instead of “mailman” or “mailwoman” conveys a powerful message: it recognizes the capabilities of individuals of either gender for delivering the mail. This seemingly minor change reflects a more extensive commitment to acknowledging the ability of every person, regardless of his or her gender. Another aspect of inclusive communication, known as person-first language, encourages us to prioritize the individual over any defining characteristic. Instead of saying “colored people,” we should use “people of color.” Similarly, opting for “person with blindness” over “blind person” highlights the unique identity and dignity of each individual while avoiding the reduction of a person to an unusual characteristic. In summary, inclusive language plays a crucial role in creating a fair and welcoming society, where every individual can embrace his or her genuine self without the fear of exclusion.
solution: ① inclusivity는 ‘포용성’이라는 뜻으로, 다양한 배경을 가진 사람들을 동등하게 포함하는 태도를 의미하므로 올바른 설명이다. ② gender-neutral은 ‘특정 성별에 치우치지 않는, 성 중립적인’이라는 뜻인데, 제시문에서는 “한 특정 성별을 선호하는”이라고 설명하고 있으므로 틀렸다. ③ prioritize는 ‘우선시하다’라는 뜻으로 적절하다. ④ crucial은 ‘매우 중요한’이라는 의미로 문맥에 맞다. ⑤ embrace는 ‘기꺼이 받아들이다’라는 뜻으로 올바른 설명이다.
choices: inclusivity : the practice of including people of different backgrounds and identities equally
gender-neutral : showing preference toward one particular gender
prioritize : to treat something as more important than other things
crucial : extremely important or necessary
embrace : to accept something willingly and positively

Katherine Johnson, a "Computer" Who Looked Beyond Numbers Katherine Johnson was born on August 26, 1918, in West Virginia, in the U.S., and was the youngest of four children in a black family. Katherine was a math prodigy from early childhood. Reflecting on her youth, Katherine once said, “I counted everything—the steps to the road, the steps up to church, the number of dishes, spoons, and forks I washed.” She excitedly added, “I couldn’t wait to get to high school to take algebra and geometry.” But Katherine’s hometown had a segregated education system, and black students could not enter high school. So her father moved the family 200 kilometers away so that she could enter high school. After graduating from high school in 1932, she was admitted to a black college at the age of fifteen. By her junior year, she had taken all the math courses the college could offer. Her mentor gladly offered special classes just for her, but he was not happy when he had to tell his outstanding student about her career opportunities. “You would make a good research mathematician,” he told his seventeen-year-old student, “and I’m going to prepare you for this career.” Katherine asked, “Where will I find a job?” “That,” he replied, “will be your problem.” The path ahead was unclear and full of obstacles, but Katherine knew she had the strength to make her own way.
solution: ① prodigy는 “특정 분야에서 뛰어난 재능을 가진 천재적인 아이(young person with exceptional talent)”라는 뜻으로, 제시된 영영 풀이가 알맞다. 본문에서도 Katherine Johnson이 어린 시절부터 뛰어난 수학 능력을 보였다고 설명한다. ② algebra는 ‘대수학’이라는 뜻인데, 제시문은 “생물과 자연환경을 연구하는 학문”이라고 설명하고 있으므로 틀렸다. 이는 biology에 가까운 설명이다. ③ geometry는 ‘기하학’이라는 뜻인데, 제시문은 “과거 사건과 인간 사회를 연구하는 학문”이라고 설명하고 있으므로 틀렸다. 이는 history의 설명에 해당한다. ④ segregate는 ‘분리하다, 차별하여 구분하다’라는 뜻인데, 제시문은 “서로 다른 집단이 평등하게 함께 일하도록 장려하다”라고 설명하고 있으므로 반대 의미이다. ⑤ obstacle은 ‘장애물, 방해물’이라는 뜻인데, 제시문은 “훌륭한 성과에 대해 주어지는 보상”이라고 설명하고 있으므로 틀렸다. 이는 reward와 유사한 의미이다.
choices: prodigy : a young person who has an unusually great ability in something
algebra : a subject that studies living things and the natural environment
geometry : the study of past events and human societies
segregate : to encourage different groups of people to work together equally
obstacle : a reward or benefit given for excellent performance

It was not until 1953 ⓐthat Katherine found a job at a NASA field center in Virginia. There, she worked as one of the “Black computers” who did complex calculations manually to support white male engineers. Though they greatly contributed to the space project, they endured a lot of discrimination, including segregation in the office and ⓑbeing referred to with terms like “girl” despite being professional women. Two weeks into the job, Katherine was reassigned to NASA’s elite space research division. There, she was the only black female member of the staff. Despite her enormous contributions, the important research meetings ⓒwere held only among white staff members. When she asked for permission to attend the meetings, her male colleagues said that “the girls” didn’t usually go. Katherine asked, “Is there a law that says I can’t go?” The ⓓembarrassed male workers had no choice but to let her in. By asking questions no one had ever asked, Katherine ended a discriminatory custom. She had faced barriers, but her efforts to overcome them paid off. She felt proud and continued her work with courage. In 1960, she wrote a research paper with another engineer about how to place a spacecraft into orbit. That was the first time a woman in her division ⓔreceiving credit as an author of a research report.

Katherine's remarkable calculations by hand were trusted more than digital computers. In early 1962, John Glenn, one of the pioneering American astronauts, was preparing to orbit the Earth for the first time in American history. NASA used an electronic computer, first introduced into the space program a year earlier, to calculate the spaceship's trajectory, but it made many minor errors. Glenn, who was concerned about its accuracy, asked Katherine Johnson to double-check the machine's figures by hand. "If she says the numbers are good," he said, "I'm good to go."

I am ready to train for the next space program.

다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.
Katherine Johnson was born on August 26, 1918, in West Virginia, in the U.S., and was the youngest of four children in a black family. Katherine was a math prodigy from early childhood. Reflecting on her youth, Katherine once said, "I counted everything – the steps to the road, the steps up to church, the number of dishes, spoons, and forks I washed." She excitedly added, "I couldn't wait to get to high school to take algebra and geometry." But Katherine's hometown had a segregated education system, and black students could not enter high school.
(A) So her father moved the family 200 kilometers away so that she could enter high school. (B) After graduating from high school in 1932, she was admitted to a black college at the age of fifteen. (C) Her mentor gladly offered special classes just for her, but he was not happy when he had to tell his outstanding student about her career opportunities. (D) "You would make a good research mathematician," he told his seventeen-year-old student, "and I'm going to prepare you for this career." Katherine asked, "Where will I find a job?" "That," he replied, "will be your problem." (E) The path ahead was unclear and full of obstacles, but Katherine knew she had the strength to make her own way. In 1935, at the age of eighteen, Katherine graduated from college with highest honors and began her career as a teacher at a black public school. At that time, teaching was the only option available to her.

윗글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적 절한 곳은?
By her junior year, she had taken all the math courses the college could offer.
solution: Katherine이 가진 능력에도 불구하고 겪었던 차별을 설명하는 내용의 글이다. 주어진 문장은 3학년 때까지 그녀는 대학이 제공할 수 있는 모든 수학 과정을 이수했다는 내용이다. 따라서 이 문장 앞에는 대학 입학 직후의 상황에 대한 문장이 있어야 하고, 뒤에는 더 이상 들을 수업이 없어 멘토가 특별 수업을 제공하게 된 문장이 이어져야 한다. 따라서 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은 ③ (C) 이다.

Language has the power to shape our attitudes and behaviors. Inclusive language serves as an important tool for acknowledging diversity, encouraging sensitivity to differences, and promoting equal opportunities. It actively contributes to breaking biases and discriminatory language and to building a (A) _____ environment of inclusivity. For example, adopting the gender-neutral term “mail carrier” instead of “mailman” or “mailwoman” conveys a powerful message: it recognizes the capabilities of individuals of either gender for delivering the mail. This seemingly minor change reflects a more extensive commitment to acknowledging the ability of every person, regardless of his or her gender. Another aspect of inclusive communication, known as person-first language, ⓐencourages us to prioritize the individual over any defining characteristic. Instead of saying “colored people,” we should use “people of color.” Similarly, opting for “person with blindness” over “blind person” highlights the unique identity and dignity of each individual while avoiding the reduction of a person to an unusual characteristic. In summary, inclusive language plays a crucial role in creating a fair and (B) _____ society, (C) [where / her / embrace / self / every / without / of / can / genuine / exclusion / or / the / his / individual / fear].

(C)에 주어진 단어들을 <보기>의 해석에 맞게 바르게 재배 열하시오.
보기 모든 개인이 배제될 두려움 없이 자신의 진정한 모 습을 드러낼 수 있는
→ _____
answer: where every individual can embrace his or her genuine self without the fear of exclusion

Katherine Johnson was born on August 26, 1918, in West Virginia, in the U.S., and was the

Reflecting on her youth, Katherine once said, "I ⓑcounted everything—the steps to the road, the steps up to church, the number of dishes, spoons, and forks I ⓒwashed." She excitedly ⓓadded, "I couldn't ⓔwait to get to high school to take algebra and geometry."
solution: ② 제시된 풀이 'to give out things to each person in a group(그룹의 각 사람에게 물건을 나눠주다)'는 count(세다) 의 뜻과 전혀 다른 개념이다. count의 올바른 풀이는 'to say or find the total number of things in a group(그룹 안의 사물의 총 수를 말하거나 구하다)'이다. 따라서 ②가 정답이다. ① youngest(막내, 가장 어린): 어떤 집단에서 가장 최근에 태어난 사람 ③ wash(씻다): 물과 비누를 사용하여 무언가를 깨끗이 하다 ④ add(덧붙이다): 이미 말해진 것에 무언가를 더 말하다 ⑤ wait(기다리다): 특정한 일이 일어날 때까지 어딘가에 머물다
choices: ⓐyoungest: a person who was born most recently among others in a group
ⓑcount: to give out things to each person in a group

body:
다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.
Katherine Johnson was born on August 26, 1918, in West Virginia, in the U.S., and was the youngest of four children in a black family. Katherine was a math prodigy from early childhood. Reflecting on her youth, Katherine once said, "I counted everything-the steps to the road, the steps up to church, the number of dishes, spoons, and forks I washed." She excitedly added, "I couldn't wait to get to high school to take algebra and geometry.“ But Katherine's hometown had a segregated education system, and black students could not enter high school. So her father moved the family 200 kilometers away so that she could enter high school. After graduating from high school in 1932, she was admitted to a black college at the age of fifteen. By her junior year, she had taken all the math courses the college could offer. Her mentor gladly offered special classes just for her, but he was not happy when he had to tell his outstanding student about her career opportunities. "You would make a good research mathematician," he told his seventeen-year-old student, "and I'm going to prepare you for this career." Katherine asked, "Where will I find a job?" "That," he replied, "will be your problem." The path ahead was unclear and full of obstacles, but Katherine knew she had the strength to make her own way. In 1935, at the age of eighteen, Katherine graduated from college with highest honors and began her career as a teacher at a black public school. At that time, teaching was the only option available to her.

윗글의 Katherine이 그녀의 멘토와의 대화 이후 느꼈을 감정으로 가장 적절한 것은?
solution: 앞길이 불투명하고 장애물이 가득했지만, Katherine은 자신만의 길을 개척할 힘이 있다는 것을 알았으므로, 그녀의 감정은 ② determined(단호한)이다.
choices: satisfied
determined
indecisive
relieved
dull

(B) She asked, "Where will I find a job?" "That," he replied, "will be your problem." The path ahead was unclear and full of obstacles, but Katherine knew she had the strength to make her own way.
(C) Her mentor gladly offered special classes just for her, but he was not happy when he had to tell his outstanding student about her career opportunities. "You would make a good research mathematician," he told his seventeen-year-old student, "and I'm going to prepare you for this career."
solution: 주니어 시절 대학의 모든 수학 과정을 마쳤다는 내용의 주어진 글 다음에는, 멘토가 특별 수업을 열며 훌륭한 연구 수학자가 될 것이라고 격려하는 내용의 (C)가 이어져야 한다. 그다음에는 취업에 대한 멘토의 현실적인 대답과 장애물 앞에서도 굴하지 않는 Katherine의 의지를 다루는 내용의 (B)가 온 후, 18세에 대학을 최우수 성적으로 졸업하고 교사로 첫 경력을 시작했다는 내용의 (A)로 마무리되는 것이 글의 순서로 가장 적절하다. 따라서 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은 ⑤이다.

다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
After graduating from high school in 1932, she was admitted to a black college at the age of fifteen. By her junior year, she had taken all the math courses the college could offer. Her mentor gladly offered special classes just for her, but he was not happy when he had to tell his outstanding student about her career opportunities. "You would make a good research mathematician," he told his seventeen-year-old student, "and I'm going to prepare you for this career." Katherine asked, "Where will I find a job?" "That," he replied, "will be your problem." The path ahead was unclear and full of obstacles due to her gender and race. In 1935, at the age of eighteen, Katherine graduated from college with highest honors and began her career as a teacher at a black public school. At that time, teaching was the only option available to her. Despite being a math prodigy who graduated with highest honors, Katherine began her career as a teacher because _____ .
solution: Katherine이 실력을 갖췄지만, 당대의 현실로 어려움을 겪는 내용으로, 그녀가 교사가 된 이유로 당시의 인종 및 성별 장벽이 직업적 선택지를 제한했다는 내용이 와야 할 것이다. 따라서 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은 ⑤ '그녀의 인종과 성별에 기반한 사회적 장벽이 그녀의 직업적 선택을 교육 분야로 제한했다’이다.
choices: she preferred teaching mathematics to young black students over research
she was too young to enter the competitive field of research and engineering
her mentor advised her that teaching was the best way to prepare for stable career
she wanted to use the salary from teaching to finance her graduate studies later
social barriers based on her race and gender limited her professional options to the teaching field

body:
다음 글에 드러난 Katherine의 성격을 묘사한 것으로 가 장 적절한 것은?
Two weeks into the job, Katherine was reassigned to NASA's elite space research division. There, she was the only black female member of the staff. Regardless of her enormous contributions, the important research meetings were held only among white staff members. When she asked for permission to attend the meetings, her male colleagues said that "the girls" didn't usually go. Katherine asked, "Is there a law that says I can't go?" The embarrassed male workers had no choice but to let her in. By asking questions no one had ever asked, Katherine ended a discriminatory custom. She had faced barriers, but her efforts to overcome them paid off. She felt proud and continued her work with confidence. In 1960, she wrote a research paper with another engineer about how to place a spacecraft into orbit. That was the first time a woman in her division received credit as an author of a research report.
solution: Katherine은 차별적 규정에 굴하지 않고 당당하게 권리를 쟁취했으므로, 성격으로 가장 적절한 것은 ⑤ '용기 있고 자신감 넘치는'이다.
choices: passive and obedient
humble and dedicated
arrogant and stubborn
cool-headed and logical
courageous and self-assured

body:
다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
Katherine's remarkable calculations by hand were trusted more than digital computers. In early 1962, John Glenn, one of the pioneering American astronauts, was preparing to orbit the Earth for the first time in American history. NASA used an electronic computer, first introduced into the space program a year earlier, to calculate the spaceship's trajectory, but it made many minor errors. Glenn, who was concerned about its accuracy, asked Katherine Johnson to double-check the machine's figures by hand. If she says the numbers are good," he said, "I'm good to go." Using only a pencil and a slide rule, Katherine spent a day and a half checking the calculations and finally made sure of them. Eventually, Glenn became the first American astronaut to orbit the Earth. Katherine was also part of the team that performed calculations for Apollo 11, which sent the first three men to the Moon in 1969, and even the plan to put people on Mars, which is still being worked on today.
solution: NASA가 우주선의 궤적을 계산하기 위해 전자 컴퓨터를 사용했으나 많은 사소한 오류들을 범했다고 했으므로, 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은 ② '나사는 우주선의 궤도를 계산하기 위해 새로운 전자 컴퓨터를 사용했으나, 몇 가지 큰 실수들을 저질렀다.'이다.

NASA used a new electronic computer to calculate the spaceship's path, but it made a few big mistakes.
Glenn told Katherine Johnson to confirm the machine's numbers by hand.

body:
다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.
It was not until 1953 that Katherine found a job at a NASA field center in Virginia. There, she worked as one of the "Black computers" who did complex calculations manually to support white male engineers. Though they greatly contributed to the space project, they endured a lot of discrimination, including segregation in the office and being referred to with terms like "girl" despite being professional women. Two weeks into the job, Katherine was reassigned to NASA's elite space research division. There, she was the only black female member of the staff. Despite her enormous contributions, the important research meetings were held only among white staff members. When she asked for permission to attend the meetings, her male colleagues said that "the girls" didn't usually go. Katherine asked, "Is there a law that says I can't go?" The embarrassed male workers had no choice but to let her in. By asking questions no one had ever asked, Katherine ended a discriminatory custom. She had faced barriers, but her efforts to overcome them paid off. She felt proud and continued her work with courage. In 1960, she wrote a research paper with another engineer about how to place a spacecraft into orbit. That was the first time a woman in her division received credit as an author of a research report. Katherine's remarkable calculations by hand were trusted more than digital computers. In early 1962, John Glenn, one of the pioneering American astronauts, was preparing to orbit the Earth for the first time in American history. NASA used an electronic computer, first introduced into the space program a year earlier, to calculate the spaceship's trajectory, but it made many minor errors. Glenn, who was concerned about its accuracy, asked Katherine Johnson to double-check the machine's figures by hand. "If she says the numbers are good," he said, "I'm good to go." Using only a pencil and a slide rule, Katherine spent a day and a half checking the calculations and finally made sure of them. Eventually, Glenn became the first American astronaut to orbit the Earth. Katherine was also part of the team that performed calculations for Apollo 11, which sent the first three men to the Moon in 1969, and even the plan to put people on Mars, which is still being worked on today. Katherine retired in 1986 after thirty-three years at NASA. After that, she dedicated the rest of her life to championing access to STEM education for Black girls. For her contributions, President Barack Obama awarded her the Presidential Medal of Freedom in 2015 and said, "Katherine G. Johnson refused to be limited by society's expectations of her gender and race while expanding the boundaries of humanity's reach." In 2017, NASA dedicated a building in her honor in Virginia and named it the Katherine G. Johnson Computational Research Facility. She died on February 24, 2020, at the age of 101, but her pioneering legacy will never be forgotten.

Language has the power to shape our attitudes and behaviors. Inclusive language serves as an important tool for acknowledging diversity, encouraging sensitivity to differences, and promoting equal opportunities. It actively contributes to breaking biases and discriminatory language and to building a welcoming environment of inclusivity. For example, adopting the gender-neutral term "mail carrier" instead of "mailman" or "mailwoman" conveys a powerful message: it recognizes the capabilities of individuals of either gender for delivering the mail. This seemingly minor change reflects a more extensive commitment to acknowledging the ability of every person, regardless of his or her gender. Another aspect of inclusive communication, known as person-first language, encourages us to prioritize the individual over any defining characteristic. Instead of saying "colored people," we should use "people of color." Similarly, opting for "person with blindness" over "blind person" highlights the unique identity and dignity of each individual while avoiding the reduction of a person to an unusual characteristic. Inclusive language is a vital tool that actively shapes perceptions by acknowledging (A) and breaking down discriminatory biases. It operates through specific strategies, such as using gender-neutral terms to focus on capability, and employing person-first language to (B) _____ the individual over their defining characteristics. Ultimately, the goal of this linguistic shift is to foster a more (C) _____ and welcoming society where everyone feels respected and free from the fear of exclusion.

If you are gripped by fear and a lack of desire (A)[speak / to speak] up in meetings, you must make an attempt to change the way you view feedback. When you start applying your new skills, you will find the presentation more enjoyable, (C)[that / which] in turn will naturally have a positive impact on your overall performance.

다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?
In 1935, at the age of eighteen, Katherine graduated from college with highest honors and began her career as a teacher at a black public school. At that time, teaching was the only option
ⓐavailable to her. It was not until 1953 that Katherine found a job at a NASA field center in Virginia. There, she worked as one of the “Black computers” who ⓑ did complex calculations manually to support white male engineers. Though they greatly contributed to the space project, they endured a lot of discrimination, including segregation in the office and ⓒbeing referred to with terms like “girl” despite being professional women. Two weeks into the job, Katherine was reassigned to NASA’s elite space research division. There, she was the only black female member of the staff. Despite her enormous contributions, the important research meetings were held only among white staff members. When she asked for permission to attend the meetings, her male colleagues said that “the girls” didn’t usually go. Katherine asked, “Is there a law that ⓓsay I can’t go?” The embarrassed male workers had no choice but to let her in. By asking questions no one had ever asked, Katherine ended a discriminatory custom. She had faced barriers, but her efforts to overcome them paid off. She felt proud and continued her work with courage. In 1960, she wrote a research paper with another engineer about how to place a spacecraft into orbit. That was the first time a woman in her division ⓔreceived credit as an author of a research report. 실전 학습
solution: ⓓ say → says 관계대명사절의 선행사는 a law(단수 명사)이므로 동사도 단수형 says가 와야 한다. Is there a law that says I can’t go? (O) Is there a law that say I can’t go? (X) ⓐ available : 형용사의 후치수식 ⓑ did : 선행사 computers에 대한 관계절 동사 ⓒ being referred : 전치사 including의 목적어 역할을 하는 동명사구 ⓔ received : 과거 사실을 나타내는 동사

(A)Language has the power to shape our attitudes and behaviors. Inclusive language serves as an important tool for acknowledging diversity, encouraging sensitivity to differences, and promoting equal opportunities. (B)It contributes to breaking biases and discriminatory language and to build an environment of inclusivity.For example, adopting the gender- neutral term "mail carrier" instead of "mailman" or "mailwoman" conveys a powerful message: it recognizes the capabilities of individuals of either gender for delivering the mail. (C)This seemingly minor _____ change reflects a more extensive commitment to acknowledging the ability of every person, regardless of his or her gender.
(D)Another aspect of inclusive communication encourages us to prioritize the individual over any defining characteristic. Instead of saying "colored people," we should use "people of color." Similarly, (E)opting for "person with blindness" over "blind person" highlights the unique identity and dignity of each individual while avoiding the reduction of a person to an unusual characteristic. In summary, (F)inclusive language plays a crucial role in creating a fair society, which every individual can embrace his or her genuine self.
조건 1. 어색한 문장의 기호(A~F)를 쓰고, 수정 부분을 포함한 밑줄 부분 전체를 쓸 것

answer: (1) (B) It contributes to breaking biases and discriminatory language and to building an environment of inclusivity. (2) (F) inclusive language plays a crucial role in creating a fair society, where every individual can embrace his or her genuine self

(2) (F) 선행사 a fair society를 수식하고 완전한 절을 이끄는 관계부사 where가 와야 하기에 which는 where로 고쳐야 하므로, 정답은 'inclusive language plays a crucial role in creating a fair society, where every individual can embrace his or her genuine self.'이다.

body:
다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.
After several rainy days, the Sun came out to shine light on Josie and her whole bed. Josie woke up and made a miraculous recovery. Seasons and years went by, and she grew into a healthy adult. ⓐ When Josie left for college, Klara was sent to the Yard, a place which old AFs spend their remaining days at the end of their lives. In the Yard, she remembered her days with Josie.
Klara: Josie was the best teenager for me. ⓑ I did all I could to learn Josie and to do that was best for her. ⓒ If it had become necessary, I could have continued Josie. But I don’t think it would have worked out so well. ⓓ Not because I wouldn’t have achieved accuracy, but however hard I tried, I believe now there would remain something beyond my reach. ⓔ Mr. Capaldi believed there was nothing special inside Josie, but I believe now that there was something very special. But it wasn’t inside Josie. It was inside those who loved her. ⓕ I would have never reached what they felt for Josie in their hearts. I am sure of this now.

<보기>의 관점에서 윗글의 Klara에 대해 보일 반응으로 적절하지 않은 것은?
보기 기계의 근본적인 목적은 인간의 필요를 충족시키 기 위함이다. 그것은 자신의 감정보다 정확한 임무 수행을 우선시해야 하며 임무의 성공 여부를 섣불 리 판단하기보다 실현 가능성을 현실적인 측면으 로 제시해야 한다.
solution: <보기>의 관점은 기계의 목적이 인간의 필요 충족이며 감정보다 정확한 임무 수행을 우선시해야 한다는 것이다. < 보기>의 관점에서 볼 때, Klara가 한계 너머에 무언가가 남아있어 자신이 도달할 수 없음을 인정하고, 이것을 확신하는 태도는 임무의 성공 가능성을 섣불리 판단한 것이다. 따라서 반응으로 적절하지 않은 것은 ⑤이다.
choices: 필요했다면 인간을 대체할 수도 있었다고 말하는 것은 인간 의 필요를 충족시키려는 기계의 근본적 목적을 지키기 위해 서야.
Josie를 잇는 일이 잘 안 되었을 것이라고 성공 가능성을 성 급히 평가하기보다, 원래의 임무를 수행하는 행위 자체에 더 집중해야 해.
한계 너머에 무엇인가가 항상 남아있을 것이라는 말은 임무 의 실현 가능성을 현실적인 측면으로 제시하는 모습이야.
반복해서 등장하는 주관적 추측과 확신은 기계가 감정을 지 나치게 앞세우는 모습으로서, 임무 수행에 지장을 줄 우려가 있어.
자신은 Josie를 사랑하는 사람들의 마음에 도달할 수 없음 을 인정함으로써, 임무의 성공 여부를 섣불리 판단하는 실수 를 범하지 않았군.

윗글의 ⓐ~ⓕ 중 어법상 적절한 문장의 개수는?
solution: ⓒ 조건문 내에서 과거 사실과 반대되는 일을 가정하는 가정법 과거완료 구문이다. ⓔ 접속사 that이 이끄는 명사절이 보어로 올바르게 쓰였다. ⓕ 조동사의 과거형 뒤에 완료형을 써서 과거에 대한 강한 추측을 나타낸다. ⓐ a place를 수식하는 표현 뒤에 절이 갖추어져 있으므로, which는 where로 고쳐야 한다. ⓑ do의 목적어 역할을 수행하면서 삽입절의 주어를 이끄는 관계대명사가 와야 하므로, that은 what으로 고쳐야 한다. ⓓ 가정법 과거완료 시제가 등위접속사 but과 동일하게 이어져 있으므로, remain은 have remained로 고쳐야 한다. 따라서 어법상 적절한 문장의 개수는 3개이다.
choices: 3개

solution: Klara는 만약 필요했다면 Josie를 이어받을 수 있겠지만, 그것이 완벽히 성공하지는 못했을 것이라고 말했다. 또한, Klara가 Josie를 이어받는 것은 기계의 희생 정신과 거리가 멀다. 따라서 적절하지 않은 반응은 ④이다.
choices: 혜송: Josie가 태양의 빛 덕분에 병을 극복하고 건강한 성인 으로 자라나게 되어서 다행이야. 나도 어떤 어려운 일이 있 어도 포기하지 않을 거야.
채린: Yard로 보내진 Klara가 Josie와의 지난날을 아름답 게 추억하는 모습을 보니 기계 역시 인간과 깊은 교감을 나 눌 수 있다는 희망을 품었어.
현지: 내 생각은 좀 반대야. 쓸모가 사라지자 버려진 것과 다 름 없잖아. AF를 도구처럼 대하는 사람들의 모습이 영 불편 해.
사랑: Klara가 자신을 희생해서 Josie를 계속 살게 했다면 벌어졌을 일을 가정한 후, 자기 한계를 넘는 것이 있음을 인 정하고 있어. 인간을 위한 기계의 희생 정신이 돋보여.
윤경: 사람을 특별하게 만드는 것은 자기 안에 있지 않고, 자 신을 사랑해주는 사람 안에 있다는 메시지가 참 감동적이 야. 나도 주변 사람을 사랑하는 마음을 전해서 그들의 삶이 가치 있음을 알려주고 싶어.

body:
다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.
Klara is an AF (Artificial Friend), a companion robot for children. She is solar-powered. She stays healthy when she gets the Sun’s nourishment but feels weak and lifeless without sunlight. At the robot store, she enjoyed
(A) [taking / to take] in the outside world from the windows. Klara closely observed what she saw, hoping to learn everything necessary to be a caring and helpful AF. One evening, she discovered (B) [that / what] a homeless man was lying on the street without moving. Klara was sad (가)as she believed he had died. But the next morning when the Sun was shining, she was (C)
[surprised / surprising] to see that the homeless man was sitting up and stroking his dog. Klara believed the Sun had saved him and came to have strong faith in the Sun’s power to restore everything.

윗글의 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 가장 적절한 표현으로 짝 지어진 것은?
solution: (A) 동사 enjoy는 동명사를 목적어로 취하므로, taking이 적절하다. (B) 뒤에 완전한 문장이 이어지며 동사 discover의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이끌어야 하므로, 접속사 that이 적절하다. (C) 주어가 감정을 느끼는 대상이므로, surprised가 적절하다.
choices: taking - that - surprised
to take - that - surprised
taking - what - surprised
to take - what - surprising
taking - that - surprising

body:
다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.
In Josie’s country home, Klara found out that Josie had gone through a procedure known as “lifting.” By being lifted, Josie’s cognitive abilities had been genetically ⓐ enhanced so that she had a better chance of getting into prestigious universities. However, Josie was suffering from serious side effects similar to those that had claimed the life of her sister, Sal. A mysterious chronic illness often caused her to stay in bed for days on end. Because of this, Josie spent most of her time at home and was being educated there.
(A) To her surprise, she saw something that looked like Josie suspended in the air—it was an AF replica of Josie’s body! As it turned out, Mr. Capaldi was not a painter but a scientist, who planned with Chrissie to transfer Klara’s consciousness to the replica and make a new Josie if the real Josie were to ⓑsurvive.
(B) One day when Josie felt better, her mother took her and Klara to the city so that Josie could have her portrait done by Mr. Capaldi. In Capaldi’s studio, Klara was asked to answer a questionnaire about Josie. Looking around the studio after ⓒcompleting the questionnaire, Klara entered Capaldi’s office.
(C) Capaldi: Klara, tell me what you think about the replica.
Klara: It ⓓresembles Josie quite accurately. Mr. Capaldi, you have done a good job of capturing Josie’s appearance. I now understand why Chrissie asked me, at every step, to ⓔobserve and learn Josie. The survey seems to test how well I have come to know Josie and how well I understand her _____ and feelings.

다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
solution: 본문에서 Mr. Capaldi는 화가가 아니라 과학자이며, Klara의 의식을 replica에 옮겨 새로운 Josie를 만들 계획을 세우고 있었다고 설명된다. 따라서 ②가 옳다. ① Josie는 lifting 이후 심각한 부작용과 만성 질환에 시달렸다. ③ Klara는 Josie에 대한 questionnaire에 답했다. ④ Josie는 대부분 집에서 교육을 받았다. ⑤ Chrissie는 오히려 Klara에게 Josie를 계속 관찰하고 배우도록 요청했다.
choices: Josie became healthier after the lifting procedure without any side effects.
Mr. Capaldi was actually a scientist rather than a painter.
Klara refused to answer questions about Josie in the studio.
Josie attended school regularly outside her home.
Chrissie wanted to stop Klara from learning about Josie.

밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
solution: ⓑ의 survive는 문맥상 어색하다. 본문에서는 “실제 Josie가 죽게 된다면(if the real Josie were to die)”이라는 의미가 와야 하므로, survive가 아니라 die가 사용되어야 자연스럽다. 따라서 ⓑ가 문맥에 맞지 않는 낱말이다. ⓐ enhanced : ‘향상된, 강화된’이라는 뜻으로, Josie의 인지 능력이 유전적으로 향상되었다는 문맥에 적절하다. ⓒ completing : ‘완료하는’이라는 의미로, 설문지를 다 작성한 뒤 사무실에 들어갔다는 흐름에 맞는다. ⓓ resembles : ‘~와 닮다’라는 뜻으로, replica가 Josie를 매우 정확하게 닮았다는 의미에 적절하다. ⓔ observe : ‘관찰하다’라는 뜻으로, Chrissie가 Klara에게 Josie를 계속 관찰하고 배우도록 했다는 내용에 알맞다.

In Capaldi’s studio, Klara was asked to answer a questionnaire about Josie. Looking around the studio after ⓒcompleting the questionnaire, Klara entered Capaldi’s office.

body:

Klara is an AF (Artificial Friend), a companion robot for children. She is solar-powered. She stays healthy when she gets the Sun’s nourishment but feels weak and lifeless without sunlight. Artificial robots should not depend on natural energy sources.
Homeless people need more help from society and technology.
Children prefer robot companions to human friends.

body:
다음 글에 드러난 Klara의 깨달음으로 가장 적절한 것은?
After several rainy days, the Sun came out to shine light on Josie and her whole bed. Josie woke up and made a miraculous recovery. Seasons and years went by, and she grew into a healthy adult. When Josie left for college, Klara was sent to the Yard, a place where old AFs spend their remaining days at the end of their lives. In the Yard, she remembered her days with Josie.
Klara: Josie was the best teenager for me. I did all I could to learn Josie and to do what was best for her. If it had become necessary, I could have continued Josie. But I don’t think it would have worked out so well. Not because I wouldn’t have achieved accuracy, but however hard I tried, I believe now there would have remained something beyond my reach. Mr. Capaldi believed there was nothing special inside Josie, but I believe now that there was something very special. But it wasn’t inside Josie. It was inside those who loved her. I would have never reached what they felt for Josie in their hearts. I am sure of this now.
solution: 클라라는 카팔디 씨(Mr. Capaldi)의 생각과 달리 조시에게 아주 특별한 무언가가 존재했지만, 그것은 조시 개인의 내면이 아니라 '조시를 사랑했던 사람들의 마음속'에 있었다고 말한다. 즉, 인간을 진정 특별하게 만드는 핵심 요소는 개인 그 자체의 물리적·기계적 특성이 아니라 타인을 향한 사랑과 감정이라는 것을 깨닫게 된다. 따라서 ②가 정답이다. ① 클라라는 아무리 노력해도 사람들의 마음속 감정에 다다를 수 없었을 것이라 고백하므로 글의 내용과 반대된다. ③ 지문에서 태양빛에 의해 조시가 기적적으로 회복된 장면은 나오지만, 의학 치료와의 비교는 언급되지 않았다. ④ Yard는 새로운 임무를 받는 곳이 아니라 오래된 AF들이 삶의 마지막 날들을 보내는 장소이다. ⑤ 클라라는 정확성을 갖추었더라도 타인의 마음속 깊은 사랑까지 대체할 수는 없었을 것이라고 밝히고 있다.
choices: 기술이 발전하면 로봇도 인간의 감정을 완벽히 지닐 수 있 다.
인간을 특별하게 만드는 것은 인간 그 자체가 아니라 타인 을 향한 사랑이다.
아픈 환자를 회복시키는 데에는 태양빛보다 의학 치료가 훨 씬 중요하다.
AF는 수명이 다하면 Yard에서 새로운 임무를 부여받는다.
완벽한 정확성만 갖추면 누군가의 삶을 완벽히 대체할 수 있다.

body:
다음 글에서 Capaldi가 'Klara가 Josie의 욕구와 열망을 이해하는 과정에 잘 도달해 있다'는 증거로 제시한 것을 본 문에서 찾아 2단어로 쓰시오.
Capaldi: Klara, tell me what you think about the replica.
Klara: It resembles Josie quite accurately. Mr. Capaldi, you have done a good job of capturing Josie’s appearance. I now understand why Chrissie asked me, at every step, to observe and learn Josie. The survey seems to test how well I have come to know Josie and how well I understand her decisions and feelings.
Capaldi: We will ask you to become her and to live in that replica of Josie with everything you have learned. Learn Josie, not just superficially, but deeply, entirely. You have to continue her for Chrissie and for everyone else who loves Josie.
Chrissie: I have doubts. I’m still not sure if this whole plan is the best thing we can do. I have been afraid of losing Josie ever since I lost Sal. That is why I agreed with you on this replica, but however well you make it, I don’t think I will be able to accept this AF as my Josie.
Capaldi: You must not lose faith, Chrissie. The survey Klara has successfully completed is clear evidence that she is already well on her way to understanding all of Josie’s drives and desires. You believe that there is something unreachable inside each of us, something that is unique and won’t transfer. But there is nothing like that. The new Josie won’t be an imitation. She will be the exact same person and you will have every right to love her just as you love Josie now.
Chrissie: But will I believe in it? When the day comes, will I really?
Klara: Excuse me, but I would like to say there 06 is a chance you will never need the new Josie. She may overcome her illness. If wrong to give up hope already.
→
solution: 본문에서 Capaldi가 Chrissie를 설득하는 대화 부분에서 'Klara가 성공적으로 작성 마친 그 설문지(The survey)는 그녀가 이미 Josie의 모든 욕구와 열망을 이해하는 과정에 잘 도달해 있다는 명확한 증거이다'라고 했으므로 Capaldi가 증거로 직접 제시한 핵심 대상은 Klara가 완료한 설문지(The survey)이다.

body:

One day, a fourteen-year-old girl named Josie visited the shop with her mother, Chrissie. Josie chatted with Klara joyfully. Josie immediately took a liking to Klara and asked whether Klara wanted to be her friend.
Josie: I really want you to come to my home. I think you’ll like my room, and we’ll see the beautiful sunset from the windows there. We can do all the great things together all the time while I’m growing up. You want to come, right?
Klara: (nodding hopefully)
Josie: That’s so good, but I want to be honest with you. I know how bad you’ll feel after people promise you perfect things and they turn out not to be so. Some days I’m not so healthy or happy. I do not know why. Do you still want to come, Klara?
Klara: If there’s anything difficult or scary, we will face it together.
→ _____ the day comes when you do need the new Josie, I will do my best to become as close to her as possible. However, it is
answer: 완벽한 조건들을 약속받은 후 그것이 사실이 아니라고 밝혀졌 을 때 상대방이 느끼게 될 상처나 나쁜 기분을 잘 알고 있어, Klara에게 실망을 주지 않기 위해서이다.
solution: 본문에서 Josie는 'I know how bad you’ll feel after people promise you perfect things and they turn out not to be so.(사람들이 완벽한 것들을 약속한 후 그것이 그렇지 않다고 밝혀졌을 때 네가 얼마나 기분이 나쁠지 안다)'라고 언급한다. 즉, 처음부터 완벽한 모습만 기대하게 했다가 나중에 건강하지 않거나 우울한 모습을 보여 클라라에게 실망이나 상처를 주는 일을 막기 위해 미리 솔직하게 고백한 것임을 알 수 있다.

body:
다음 글에 등장하는 'lifting'이란 절차가 가져온 (1) 긍정 적 결과와 (2) 부정적 결과를 지문의 내용을 바탕으로 각각 우리말로 서술하시오.
To show that she would do her best to be Josie’s friend, Klara held her hands together and shook them slightly. Pleased by Klara’s gesture of friendship, Josie asked Chrissie for her permission to buy the AF. Chrissie asked Klara what she had observed about Josie, and found Klara to be highly observant. After requesting that Klara continue to care about Josie, Chrissie agreed to buy Klara and took her home. In Josie’s country home, Klara found out that Josie had gone through a procedure known as “lifting.” By being lifted, Josie’s cognitive abilities had been genetically enhanced so that she had a better chance of getting into prestigious universities. However, Josie was suffering from serious side effects similar to those that had claimed the life of her sister, Sal. A mysterious chronic illness often caused her to stay in bed for days on end. Because of this, Josie spent most of her time at home and was being educated there.
→
answer: (1) 긍정적 결과: 유전자 조작을 통해 인지 능력이 향상되어 명 문 대학에 진학할 수 있는 더 좋은 기회를 갖게 되었다. (2) 부정적 결과: 심각한 부작용과 원인을 알 수 없는 만성 질 환에 시달려 며칠씩 누워 지내야 했고, 집에서 교육을 받아야 했다.
solution: (1) 지문의 'By being lifted, Josie’s cognitive abilities had been genetically enhanced so that she had a better chance of getting into prestigious universities.'에서 'lifting'을 받음으로써 Josie의 인지 능력이 유전적으로 강화되었고, 그 결과 명문대에 진학할 확률 (기회)이 높아졌다는 긍정적 결과를 알 수 있다. (2) 지문의 'However, Josie was suffering from serious side effects similar to those that had claimed the life of her sister, Sal. A mysterious chronic illness often caused her to stay in bed for days on end.'에서 인지 능력이 향상된 대신, 언니 Sal의 목숨을 앗아갔던 것과 유사한 심각한 부작용을 겪게 되었고 이로 인해 정체불명의 만성 질환에 시달리며 며칠 동안 침대에 누워 지내고 집에서 교육을 받아야 하는 부정적 결과를 알 수 있다.

At the robot store, she enjoyed taking in the outside world from the windows. Klara closely observed what she saw, hoping to learn everything necessary to be a caring and helpful AF. One evening, she discovered that a homeless man was lying on the street without moving. Klara was sad as she believed he had died. But the next morning when the Sun was shining, she was surprised to see that the homeless man was sitting up and stroking his dog. Klara believed the Sun had saved him and came to have strong faith in the Sun’s power to restore everything.

answer: 어느 날 저녁 움직이지 않고 길에 누워 있어 죽은 줄 알았던 노 숙인이, 다음 날 아침 햇살이 비추자 일어나 앉아 개를 쓰다듬 고 있는 모습을 직접 보았기 때문이다.
solution: 본문에서 클라라는 어느 날 저녁 길거리에 움직임 없이 누워 있는 노숙인을 보고 그가 죽었다고 생각하며 슬퍼했다. 그러나 다음 날 아침 햇빛이 비추었을 때, 그 노숙인이 다시 깨어나 앉아서 개를 쓰다듬는 장면을 목격하게 된다. 태양광으로 충전되는 로봇인 클라라는 이 놀라운 변화를 보고 태양이 죽은 줄 알았던 노숙인을 구원하고 살려냈다고 결론지으며, 모든 것을 회복시키는 태양의 힘을 강하게 신뢰하게 되었다.

다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
Imagine a child who can speak more than ten languages or a child who demonstrates surprising mathematical skills. These unusually talented children may seem like something out of a science-fiction novel, but gene-editing technology has the potential to transform such fiction into reality. The CRISPR gene-editing tool, introduced in 2012, was developed to cure previously incurable diseases by targeting and modifying specific genes. While this may seem promising, applying this technology to unborn babies raises ethical and social problems. For example, the birth of customized babies could intensify social unfairness if these techniques are only accessible to rich individuals or countries. Moreover, CRISPR can introduce errors during editing, potentially affecting an individual's future health. Though technology may continue to improve, it has not yet achieved error-free accuracy. In conclusion, while CRISPR offers potential benefits, we must use it carefully and ethically. Responsible research and comprehensive guidelines are crucial to _____ the ethical issues surrounding this innovative technology. It is important to ensure that gene editing's potential is employed for the greater good while reducing the risk of unexpected results.
solution: 빈칸 앞에서 책임 있는 연구와 포괄적 지침이 중요하다고 밝히고 있으며, 빈칸 뒤에서는 혁신적 기술을 둘러싼 윤리적 문제들이 언급되고 있다. 이 흐름상 빈칸에는 윤리적 문제들을 '다루다'는 의미의 표현이 와야 하며, 글 전체가 CRISPR의 윤리적·신중한 사용을 촉구하는 방향으로 전개되고 있다. 따라서 ① 'handling'이 흐름상 가장 자연스럽다. YBM(김) 4과 실전 모의고사 1회차

solution: 주어진 글은 열 개 이상의 언어를 구사하거나 놀라운 수학 실력을 지닌 아이를 상상하게 하며, 유전자 편집 기술이 이러한 공상과학 소설 같은 상상을 현실로 바꿀 가능성이 있다는 화제를 제시한다. The CRISPR Gene-Editing Tool Imagine a child who can speak more than ten languages or a child who demonstrates surprising mathematical skills. These unusually talented children may seem like something out of a science-fiction novel, but gene-editing technology has the potential to transform such fiction into reality. The CRISPR gene-editing tool, introduced in 2012, was developed to cure previously incurable diseases by targeting and modifying specific genes. While this may seem promising, applying this technology to unborn babies raises ethical and social problems. For example, the birth of customized babies could intensify social unfairness if these techniques are only accessible to rich individuals or countries. Moreover, CRISPR can introduce errors during editing, potentially affecting an individual’s future health. Though technology may continue to improve, it has not yet achieved error-free accuracy. In conclusion, while CRISPR offers potential benefits, we must use it carefully and ethically. Responsible research and comprehensive guidelines are crucial to handling the ethical issues surrounding this innovative technology. It is important to ensure that gene editing’s potential is employed for the greater good while reducing the risk of unexpected results.
solution: ② incurable은 ‘치료할 수 없는, 불치의’라는 뜻으로, “previously incurable diseases”라는 본문 표현에서 질병을 치료할 수 없다는 의미로 올바르게 사용되었다. 반면 나머지 영영 풀이는 실제 의미와 다르다. ① demonstrate는 ‘보여 주다, 입증하다’라는 뜻인데, 제시된 풀이에서는 ‘숨기다’라고 설명하여 틀렸다. ③ ethical은 ‘윤리적인, 도덕적으로 옳은’이라는 의미인데, 해로운 행동을 뜻한다고 설명하여 부적절하다. ④ comprehensive는 ‘포괄적인, 종합적인’이라는 뜻인데, ‘짧고 중요한 세부 사항이 부족한’이라고 설명해 틀렸다. ⑤ innovative는 ‘혁신적인, 새로운 아이디어를 도입하는’ 이라는 의미인데, ‘구식의’라고 설명하여 반대 의미가 되었다.
choices: demonstrate : to hide something from other people
incurable : impossible to cure or heal
ethical : causing harm or unfair treatment to others
comprehensive : very short and lacking important details
innovative : old-fashioned and unwilling to change 유형보충독해

Imagine a child who can speak more than ten languages or a child who demonstrates surprising mathematical skills. answer: ⓑ apply → applying (또는 To apply), ⓓ ensuring → to ensure
solution: ⓑ apply → applying (또는 To apply) 접속사 While이 이끄는 절 안에서 동사 raises(야기한다)의 주어 역할을 해야 하는 자리이다. 동사원형 apply는 문장의 주어가 될 수 없으므로 동명사 applying이나 to부정사인 To apply로 고쳐야 한다. ⓓ ensuring → to ensure 문장 앞의 It은 가주어이며, ⓓ 이하 문장이 진주어 역할을 해야 한다. 가주어-진주어 구문에서 진주어로 쓰일 때 일반적으로 to부정사가 오므로 to ensure로 고쳐야 한다. ⓐ 상태/감각 동사 seem 뒤에서 주어를 설명하는 보어 자리로, promising이 '유망한/기대를 품게 하는'이라는 의미의 형용사로 올바르게 쓰였다. ⓒ 동사 continue는 to부정사와 동명사를 모두 목적어로 취할 수 있으므로 to improve는 어법상 올바르다. ⓔ 접속사 while 뒤에 '주어+be동사(it is)'가 생략된 접속사를 남겨둔 분사구문이다. 능동의 의미로 목적어(the risk...)를 취하고 있으므로 현재분사 reducing이 올바르다.

다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.
One day, a fourteen-year-old girl named Josie visited the shop with her mother, Chrissie. Josie chatted with Klara joyfully. Josie immediately took a liking to Klara and asked whether Klara (A) (wanted / wanting) to be her friend.
Josie: I really want you to come to my home. I think you’ll like my room, and we’ll see the beautiful sunset from the windows there. We can do all the great things together all the time while I’m growing up. You want to come, right?
Klara: (nodding hopefully)
Josie: That’s so good, but I want to be honest with you. I know how bad you’ll feel after people promise you perfect things and they turn out not to (B) (be / being) so. Some days I’m not so healthy or happy. I do not know why. Do you still want to come, Klara?
Klara: If there’s anything difficult or scary, we will face it together. To show that she would do her best to be Josie’s friend, Klara held her hands together and shook them slightly. Pleased by Klara’s gesture of friendship, Josie asked Chrissie for her permission to buy the AF. Chrissie asked Klara what she had observed about Josie, and found Klara (C) (being / to be) highly observant. After requesting that Klara continue to care about Josie, Chrissie agreed to buy Klara and took her home.

다음 글의 내용으로 알 수 있는 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?
solution: 본문에서 Chrissie는 Klara가 Josie에 대해 관찰한 내용을 듣고 Klara가 매우 관찰력이 뛰어나다고 생각했다. 따라서 ④가 옳다. ① Josie는 어머니 Chrissie와 함께 가게를 방문했다. ② Klara는 Josie와 함께 가고 싶어 했다. ③ Josie는 자신이 항상 건강하거나 행복한 것은 아니라고 말했다. ⑤ 로봇을 사 달라고 요청한 사람은 Josie이다.
choices: Josie visited the robot shop alone.
Klara refused to go home with Josie.
Josie said she was always healthy and happy.
Chrissie was impressed by Klara’s careful observations about Josie.
Klara asked Chrissie for permission to buy a robot. 2회차 실전 모의고사

body:
밑줄 친 우리말 문장을 <조건>에 맞게 영작하시오.
One day, a fourteen-year-old girl named Josie visited the shop with her mother, Chrissie. Josie chatted with Klara joyfully. Josie immediately took a liking to Klara and Klara가 자신의 친구가 되고 싶어 하는지 물었다.
Josie: I really want you to come to my home. I think you’ll like my room, and we’ll see the beautiful sunset from the windows there. We can do all the great things together all the time while I’m growing up. You want to come, right?
Klara: (nodding hopefully)
Josie: That’s so good, but I want to be honest with you. I know how bad you’ll feel after people promise you perfect things and they turn out not to be so. Some days I’m not so healthy or happy. I do not know why. Do you still want to come, Klara?
Klara: If there’s anything difficult or scary, we will face it together.
조건 1. want, ask를 모두 포함하되, 필요시 단어를 변형할 것
2. 명사절 접속사를 사용할 것
3. 총 8단어로 쓸 것
→ 2회차 실전 모의고사
answer: asked whether Klara wanted to be her friend (또는 asked if Klara wanted to be her friend)
solution: ~인지 아닌지 물었다'는 불확실한 내용을 물어보는 간접의문문 형식이므로, 명사절 접속사 whether 또는 if(~ 인지 아닌지)를 사용하고 시제에 맞춰 asked whether[if] ~ 로 나타낸다. 'Klara가 자신의 친구가 되기를 원하다'는 'want + to부정사'를 사용하고 시제에 맞춰 'Klara wanted to be her friend'로 써서 asked whether Klara wanted to be her friend로 영작을 완성한다.

body:
글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절 한 곳을 고르시오.
But I don't think it would have worked out so well. After several rainy days, the Sun came out to shine light on Josie and her whole bed. Josie woke up and made a miraculous recovery. Seasons and years went by, and she grew into a healthy adult. When Josie left for college, Klara was sent to the Yard, a place where old AFs spend their remaining days at the end of their lives. In the Yard, she remembered her days with Josie.
Klara: Josie was the best teenager for me. ( ⓐ ) I did all I could to learn Josie and to do what was best for her. ( ⓑ ) If it had become necessary, I could have continued Josie. ( ⓒ ) Not because I wouldn't have achieved accuracy, but however hard I tried, I believe now there would have remained something beyond my reach. (
ⓓ ) Mr. Capaldi believed there was nothing special inside Josie, but I believe now that there was something very special. But it wasn't inside Josie. It was inside those who loved her. ( ⓔ ) I would have never reached what they felt for Josie in their hearts. I am sure of this now.
solution: 주어진 문장 'But I don't think it would have worked out so well.'은 역접 담화 표지 'But'으로 시작하여 앞에서 제시된 어떤 가능성에 대해 부정적인 평가를 내리는 내용이다. 따라서 이 문장 앞에는 Klara가 Josie를 '계속할 수 있었다'는 가능성이 제시되어야 하고, 이 문장 뒤에는 그것이 잘 되지 않았을 이유에 대한 설명이 이어져야 한다. ⓒ 앞 문장은 'If it had become necessary, I could have continued Josie.'로, Klara가 Josie를 대신할 수 있었다는 가능성을 언급하고 있으며, ⓒ 뒤 문장은 'Not because I wouldn't have achieved accuracy, but however hard I tried, I believe now there would have remained something beyond my reach.'로 잘 되지 않았을 이유를 설명하고 있다. 따라서 주어진 문장은 ⓒ 자리에 들어가는 것이 자연스럽다.

body:

Josie's health took a turn for the worse after she returned from the city. This made Klara determined to do everything she could for Josie. Klara remembered the barn into which the Sun had disappeared when she and Josie had been watching the sunset in Josie's room. Believing it to be the Sun's resting place, Klara visited there to pray to the Sun for Josie's recovery.
Klara: You must be so tired, and I'm very sorry to disturb you, but I have come here this evening to ask a special favor. I have never forgotten how strong your power to restore everything is. Josie is becoming weaker and weaker each day. Please send Josie the special nourishment she so desperately requires as you did that day to the homeless man. The Sun was then sinking into the ground, but Klara could tell he was smiling at her as he went down for his nightly rest. Out of gratitude and respect, Klara continued to look at the Sun until his last light vanished into the ground.
solution: ③ 본문은 Klara가 태양에게 Josie를 위한 특별한 자양분을 보내달라고 부탁하면서 노숙자에게 그랬던 것처럼 해달라고 언급할 뿐, 노숙자가 왜 태양의 자양분을 필요로 했는지에 대한 이유는 전혀 설명하지 않으므로 답할 수 없다. ① 본문 첫 문장에서 Josie가 도시에서 돌아온 후 건강이 나빠졌다고 했으므로 Josie가 어디에 있다가 돌아왔는지 답할 수 있다. ② Klara가 그 헛간을 태양의 휴식처라고 믿었다는 내용이 명시되어 있으므로 답할 수 있다. ④ 태양이 내려가는 동안 Klara에게 미소 짓고 있었다는 내용이 있으므로 답할 수 있다. ⑤ Klara가 태양의 마지막 빛이 땅속으로 사라질 때까지 바라보았다는 내용이 있으므로 답할 수 있다.
choices: Where had Josie been before her health got worse?
What did Klara believe the barn to be?
Why did the homeless man need the Sun's nourishment?
What was the Sun doing as he went down for his rest?
How long did Klara keep looking at the Sun?

밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 어색한 것을 모두 찾아 기호를 적고 옳게 고쳐 쓰시오.
After several rainy days, the Sun came out to shine light on Josie and her whole bed. Josie woke up and made a miraculous recovery. Seasons and years went by, and she grew into a healthy adult. When Josie left for college, Klara was sent to the Yard, a place ⓐwhere old AFs spend their remaining days at the end of their lives. In the Yard, she remembered her days with Josie.
Klara: Josie was the best teenager for me. I did all I could to learn Josie and to do ⓑwhat was best for her. If it had become necessary, I
ⓒcould continued Josie. But I don't think it would have worked out so well. Not because I wouldn't have achieved accuracy, but ⓓhowever hardly I tried, I believe now there would have remained something beyond my reach. Mr. Capaldi believed there was nothing special inside Josie, but I believe now that there was something very special. But it wasn't inside Josie. It was inside those who loved her. I would have never reached ⓔwhat they felt for Josie in their hearts. I am sure of this now.
→
answer: ⓒ could continued → could have continued, ⓓ however hardly → however hard
solution: ⓒ could continued → could have continued 조건절 If it had become necessary(had p.p.)와 호응하는 가정법 과거완료 구문이다. 과거 사실에 대한 반대 상황을 표현해야 하므로 주절의 조동사 뒤에는 동사원형이 아닌 have p.p.가 와서 could have continued가 되어야 한다. ⓓ however hardly → however hard '아무리 ~할지라도'라는 양보의 부사절을 이끄는 복합관계부사 구문(however + 형용사/부사 + 주어 + 동사) 이다. 동사 tried(노력하다)를 수식하여 '아무리 열심히 노력했을지라도'라는 의미를 만들어야 하므로 부사 hard가 와야 한다. hardly는 '거의 ~않다'라는 부정을 나타내므로 문맥과 어법에 맞지 않다. ⓐ 장소 선행사 a place 뒤에 'old AFs(주어) + spend(동사) + their remaining days(목적어)'의 완전한 절이 연결되므로 관계부사 where가 올바르게 쓰였다. ⓑ 선행사를 포함하여 do의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이끌며, 뒤에 주어가 없는 불완전한 절이 이어지므로 관계대명사인 what이 올바르게 쓰였다. ⓔ 선행사를 포함하여 reached의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이끌며, 뒤에 목적어가 빠진 불완전한 절이 이어지므로 관계대명사인 what이 올바르게 쓰였다.

다음 글을 읽고 대답할 수 없는 질문은?
In Josie's country home, Klara found out that Josie had gone through a procedure known as "lifting." By being lifted, Josie's cognitive abilities had been genetically enhanced so that she had a better chance of getting into prestigious universities. However, Josie was suffering from serious side effects similar to those that had claimed the life of her sister, Sal. A mysterious chronic illness often caused her to stay in bed for days on end. Because of this, Josie spent most of her time at home and was being educated there. One day when Josie felt better, her mother took her and Klara to the city so that Josie could have her portrait done by Mr. Capaldi. In Capaldi's studio, Klara was asked to answer a questionnaire about Josie. Looking around the studio after completing the questionnaire, Klara entered Capaldi's office. To her surprise, she saw something that looked like Josie suspended in the air—it was an AF replica of Josie's body! As it turned out, Mr. Capaldi was not a painter but a scientist, who planned with Chrissie to transfer Klara's consciousness to the replica and make a new Josie if the real Josie were to die.
solution: ② 본문은 Josie가 'lifting'으로 인해 심각한 부작용을 겪고 있다는 사실만 서술할 뿐, 왜 그 시술이 그러한 부작용을 초래했는지 그 원인이나 이유는 전혀 설명하지 않으므로, 부작용이 발생한 이유를 묻는 질문에는 답할 수 없다. ① 본문 첫 문장에서 Josie가 'lifting'이라는 시술을 받았다고 했으므로 어떤 시술을 받았는지 묻는 질문에 답할 수 있다. ③ Josie의 상태가 나아진 어느 날 어머니가 Josie와 Klara를 도시로 데려가 Capaldi에게 초상화를 그리게 했다고 명시되어 있으므로 답할 수 있다. ④ Klara가 Capaldi의 사무실에서 공중에 떠 있는 Josie와 똑같이 생긴 AF 복제본을 발견했다고 서술되어 있으므로 답할 수 있다. ⑤ 본문 마지막 문장에서 Capaldi와 Chrissie가 진짜 Josie가 죽을 경우 Klara의 의식을 복제본에 이식해 새로운 Josie를 만들 계획이었다고 밝히고 있으므로 답할 수 있다. Why did Josie's lifting procedure result in such serious side effects?
Where did Josie's mother take her and Klara one day when Josie felt better?

What did Mr. Capaldi and Chrissie plan to do if the real Josie were to die?

Imagine a child who can speak more than ten languages or a child who demonstrates surprising mathematical skills. These unusually talented children may seem like something out of a science-fiction novel, but gene-editing technology has the potential to transform such fiction into reality. The CRISPR gene-editing tool, ⓐintroduced in 2012, was developed to cure previously incurable diseases by targeting and modifying specific genes. While this may seem ⓑpromising, applying this technology to unborn babies ⓒraise ethical and social problems. For example, the birth of customized babies could intensify social unfairness if these techniques are only accessible to rich individuals or countries. Moreover, CRISPR can introduce errors during editing, potentially
ⓓaffected an individual’s future health. Though technology may continue to improve, it has not yet achieved error-free accuracy. In conclusion, while CRISPR offers potential benefits, we must use it carefully and ethically. Responsible research and comprehensive guidelines are crucial to ⓔhandle the ethical issues surrounding this innovative technology. It is important ⓕto ensure that gene editing’s potential is employed for the greater good while
ⓖreducing the risk of unexpected results.
solution: ⓒ raise → raises While절 안에서 주어는 동명사구인 applying this technology to unborn babies이다. 동명사 주어는 단수 취급하므로 단수 동사 raises로 고쳐야 한다. ⓓ affected → affecting 주절(CRISPR can introduce errors during editing) 뒤에 이어지는 분사구문이다. '개인의 미래 건강에 영향을 미치면서'라는 능동의 의미를 나타내고 뒤에 목적어(an individual's future health)가 오므로 현재분사 affecting으로 고쳐야 한다. ⓔ handle → handling be crucial to 구문에서 to는 부정사가 아닌 전치사이다. 따라서 뒤에 동사원형이 아닌 동명사 handling이 올바른 형태이다. ⓐ 주어인 The CRISPR gene-editing tool을 수식하는 과거분사로, '2012년에 소개된/도입된 도구'라는 수동의 의미이므로 introduced가 올바르다. ⓑ 감각/상태 동사 seem 뒤에서 보어 역할을 하는 형용사 (유망한, 기대를 갖게 하는)로 promising이 올바르게 쓰였다. ⓕ 가주어 It에 대응하는 진주어 역할을 하는 to부정사 구문으로 to ensure가 올바르게 쓰였다. ⓖ 접속사 while 뒤에 주어+be동사(it is)가 생략된 접속사를 남겨둔 분사구문 형태이다. 능동의 의미로 목적어(the risk...) 를 취하고 있으므로 현재분사 reducing이 올바르다.

다음 글에 드러난 필자의 태도로 가장 적절한 것은?
Imagine a child who can speak more than ten languages or a child who demonstrates surprising mathematical skills. These unusually talented children may seem like something out of a science-fiction novel, but gene-editing technology has the potential to transform such fiction into reality. The CRISPR gene-editing tool, introduced in 2012, was developed to cure previously incurable diseases by targeting and modifying specific genes. While this may seem promising, applying this technology to unborn babies raises ethical and social problems. For example, the birth of customized babies could intensify social unfairness if these techniques are only accessible to rich individuals or countries. Moreover, CRISPR can introduce errors during editing, potentially affecting an individual's future health. Though technology may continue to improve, it has not yet achieved error-free accuracy. In conclusion, while CRISPR offers potential benefits, we must use it carefully and ethically. Responsible research and comprehensive guidelines are crucial to handling the ethical issues surrounding this innovative technology. It is important to ensure that gene editing's potential is employed for the greater good while reducing the risk of unexpected results.

Imagine a child who can speak more than ten languages or a child who demonstrates surprising mathematical skills. These unusually talented children may seem like something out of a science-fiction novel, but gene-editing technology has the potential to transform such fiction into reality. The CRISPR gene-editing tool, introduced in 2012, was developed to cure previously incurable diseases by targeting and modifying specific genes. While this may seem promising, 이 기술을 태어나지 않은 아기들에게 적용하는 것은 윤리적이고 사회 적인 문제들을 야기한다. For example, the birth of customized babies could intensify social unfairness if these techniques are only accessible to rich individuals or countries. Moreover, CRISPR can introduce errors during editing, potentially affecting an individual's future health. Though technology may continue to improve, it has not yet achieved error-free accuracy.
In conclusion, while CRISPR offers potential benefits, we must use it carefully and ethically. Responsible research and comprehensive guidelines are crucial to handling the ethical issues surrounding this innovative technology. It is important to ensure that gene editing's potential is employed for the greater good while reducing the risk of unexpected results.
보기 raise / technology / this / ethical / social / problems / and / to / unborn babies / apply
조건 1. 보기의 단어들만 모두 사용하되, 필요시 단어 의 형태를 변형할 것
2. 동명사를 주어로 사용할 것
→
answer: applying this technology to unborn babies raises ethical and social problems
solution: 이 문장은 '이 기술을 적용하는 것은(주어) + 태아에게 (수식어구) + 야기한다(동사) + 윤리적·사회적 문제들을 (목적어)'의 구조로 써야 한다. 우선 '이 기술을 적용하는 것'이라는 주어를 만들기 위해 동사 apply를 동명사 applying으로 바꾸고, 적용 대상을 뜻하는 to unborn babies를 붙여 applying this technology to unborn babies라는 동명사 주어구를 만든다. 이어서 '야기한다'에 해당하는 동사를 배치할 때, 동명사 주어는 단수 취급하므로 바로 앞의 복수 명사(unborn babies)에 유의하여 raise를 단수 동사 raises로 형태를 변형해야 한다. 마지막으로 동사의 목적어로 '윤리적이고 사회적인 문제들'을 뜻하는 ethical and social problems를 차례대로 연결하여 전체 문장을 올바르게 완성한다.

다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.
One day when Josie felt better, her mother took her and Klara to the city so that Josie could have her portrait done by Mr. Capaldi. In Capaldi's studio, Klara was asked to answer a questionnaire about Josie. Looking around the studio after completing the ⓐquestionnaire, Klara entered Capaldi's office. To her surprise, she saw something that looked like Josie ⓑsuspended in the air - it was an AF replica of Josie's body! As it turned out, Mr. Capaldi was not a painter but a scientist, who planned with Chrissie to transfer Klara's consciousness to the replica and make a new Josie if the real Josie were to die.
Capaldi: Klara, (A) _____
Klara: It resembles Josie quite accurately. Mr. Capaldi, you have done a good job of ⓒcapturing Josie's appearance. I now understand why Chrissie asked me, at every step, to observe and learn Josie. The survey seems to test how well I have come to know Josie and how well I understand her decisions and feelings.
Capaldi: We will ask you to become her and to live in that replica of Josie with everything you have learned. Learn Josie, not just ⓓsuperficially, but deeply, entirely. You have to continue her for Chrissie and for everyone else who loves Josie.
Chrissie: (B) _____ I'm still not sure if this whole plan is the best thing we can do. I have been afraid of losing Josie ever since I lost Sal. That is why I agreed with you on this replica, but however well you make it, I don't think I will be able to accept this AF as my Josie.
Capaldi: You must not lose faith, Chrissie. The survey Klara has successfully completed is clear evidence that she is already well on her way to understanding all of Josie's drives and desires. You believe that there is something unreachable inside each of us, something that is unique and won't transfer. But there is nothing like that. The new Josie won't be an imitation. She will be the exact same person and you will have every right to love her just as you love Josie now.
Chrissie: But will I believe in it? When the day comes, will I really?
Klara: Excuse me, but I would like to say there is a chance you will never need the new Josie. She may ⓔovercome her illness. If the day comes when you do need the new Josie, I will do my best to become as close to her as possible. However, it is wrong to give up hope already.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ의 영영 풀이 의미가 문맥상 어색한것은?
solution: ③ capture(정확히 포착하다)는 '무력으로 소유하거나 통제하다'의 의미로 문맥상 어색하다.
choices: ⓐquestionnaire: a written set of questions that are given to people in order to collect facts or opinions about something
ⓑsuspend: to hang something so that it is free on all sides except at the point of support
ⓒcapture: to take into one's possession or control by force
ⓓsuperficially: as to the outward appearance only; on the surface
ⓔovercome: to successfully deal with or gain control of (something difficult)

One day when Josie felt better, her mother took her and Klara to the city so that Josie could have her portrait done by Mr. Capaldi. In Capaldi's studio, Klara was asked to answer a questionnaire about Josie. Looking around the studio after completing the ⓐquestionnaire, Klara entered Capaldi's office. To her surprise, she saw something that looked like Josie ⓑsuspended in the air - it was an AF replica of Josie's body! As it turned out, Mr. Capaldi was not a painter but a scientist, who planned with Chrissie to transfer Klara's consciousness to the replica and make a new Josie if the real Josie were to die.
Capaldi: Klara, (A) _____
Klara: It resembles Josie quite accurately. Mr. Capaldi, you have done a good job of ⓒcapturing Josie's appearance. I now understand why Chrissie asked me, at every step, to observe and learn Josie. The survey seems to test how well I have come to know Josie and how well I understand her decisions and feelings.
Capaldi: We will ask you to become her and to live in that replica of Josie with everything you have learned. Learn Josie, not just ⓓsuperficially, but deeply, entirely. You have to continue her for Chrissie and for everyone else who loves Josie.
Chrissie: (B) _____ I'm still not sure if this whole plan is the best thing we can do. I have been afraid of losing Josie ever since I lost Sal. That is why I agreed with you on this replica, but however well you make it, I don't think I will be able to accept this AF as my Josie.
Capaldi: You must not lose faith, Chrissie. The survey Klara has successfully completed is clear evidence that she is already well on her way to understanding all of Josie's drives and desires. You believe that there is something unreachable inside each of us, something that is unique and won't transfer. But there is nothing like that. The new Josie won't be an imitation. She will be the exact same person and you will have every right to love her just as you love Josie now.
Chrissie: But will I believe in it? When the day comes, will I really?
Klara: Excuse me, but I would like to say there is a chance you will never need the new Josie. She may ⓔovercome her illness. If the day comes when you do need the new Josie, I will do my best to become as close to her as possible. However, it is wrong to give up hope already.

다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.
Klara is an AF (Artificial Friend), a companion robot for children. She is solar-powered. She stays healthy when she gets the Sun's nourishment but feels weak and lifeless without sunlight. At the robot store, she enjoyed taking in the outside world from the windows. Klara closely observed what she saw, hoping to learn everything necessary to be a caring and helpful AF. One evening, she discovered that a homeless man was lying on the street without moving. Klara was sad as she believed he had died. But the next morning when the Sun was shining, she was surprised to see that the homeless man was sitting up and stroking his dog. Klara believed the Sun had saved him and came to have strong faith in the Sun's power to restore everything. One day, a fourteen-year-old girl named Josie visited the shop with her mother, Chrissie. Josie chatted with Klara joyfully. Josie immediately took a liking to Klara and asked whether Klara wanted to be her friend. Josie told Klara that she really wanted ⓐher to come home with them. She assured Klara that Klara would like Josie's room, where they could see the beautiful sunset from the windows. She added that they could do great things together all the time while she was growing up, and
ⓑshe asked if Klara wanted to come. Klara nodded hopefully. Josie said that she was glad to hear that but wanted to be honest. She explained that she knew how disappointing it felt when people promised perfect things that later turned out not to be so. Continuing, she confessed that some days she was not healthy or happy and that ⓒshe did not know the reason. She then asked Klara if ⓓshe still wanted to come. Klara replied that if there was anything difficult or scary, they would face it together. To show that ⓔshe would do her best to be Josie's friend, Klara held her hands together and shook them slightly. Pleased by Klara's gesture of friendship, Josie asked Chrissie for ⓕher permission to buy the AF. Chrissie asked Klara what ⓖshe had observed about Josie, and found Klara to be highly observant. After requesting that Klara continue to care about Josie, Chrissie agreed to buy Klara and took her home. In Josie's country home, Klara found out that Josie had gone through a procedure known as "lifting." By being lifted, Josie's cognitive abilities had been genetically enhanced so that she had a better chance of getting into prestigious universities. However, Josie was suffering from serious side effects similar to those that had claimed the life of ⓗher older sister, Sal. A mysterious chronic illness often caused her to stay in bed for days on end. Because of this, Josie spent most of her time at home and was being educated there.

윗글을 영화로 각색할 때 다음의 밑줄 친 (A)의 방법에 따 라 연출된 장면으로 가장 적절한 것은?
Adapting a literary work like Klara and the Sun into a feature film is not merely an act of translation, but one of transformation. A novel relies on inner thoughts and descriptive writing, whereas cinema relies on visual action and implied meanings. To bridge this gap, screenwriters employ diverse techniques. For the purpose of analysis, we can identify two contrasting approaches to scene construction. The first approach is the foundation of faithfulness. It involves constructing scenes by expanding upon specific descriptions and dialogue found directly in the source text. For instance, if a novel describes a character's physical gesture or a specific line of dialogue, the director visualizes this moment to respect the author's original vision. These scenes serve as the narrative anchors, providing the audience with recognizable moments that confirm their experience of the book. However, a strict dependence on explicit text can leave emotional gaps in a visual medium. Cinema often requires showing what is internal. Consequently, (A)the second approach involves developing scenes based on unwritten context that can be logically inferred to aid audience immersion. In this process, filmmakers expand from the novel's themes or implied backstories to show events that the author may have skipped but are essential for cinematic flow.
① In the scene, the camera captures the street outside the store window. It is early morning. The homeless man, whom Klara thought was dead, is covered in bright sunlight. He stretches his arms, sits up on the ground, and happily pets his dog. Klara watches from the window, her expression changing from sadness to amazement as she sees the sunlight waking him up.
② In the scene, Josie leans in close to Klara, her voice dropping to a whisper. The joy on her face fades into a look of vulnerability. She looks directly into Klara's eyes and admits that she isn't always happy or healthy. She tells Klara that people often make promises they can't keep.
solution: 밑줄 친 (A) '두 번째 접근'은 '텍스트에 명시되지 않았으나 논리적으로 추론 가능한 배경이나 사건을 확장하여 연출하는 방식'을 가리키므로, 정답은 ④ '씬에서, 카메라는 어두운 방의 병동 옆에 앉아 있는 Chrissie의 플래시백을 보여준다. 그녀의 나이 든 딸인 Sal이 창백한 얼굴로 숨쉬려 애쓰며 침대에 누워 있다. 눈물이 얼굴에 흐르고, 완전히 무력해 보이는 Chrissie는 Sal의 손을 꼭 붙잡는다.'이다.

(A) One day when Josie felt better, her mother took her and Klara to the city so that Josie could have her portrait done by Mr. Capaldi. In Capaldi's studio, Klara was asked to answer a questionnaire about Josie. Looking around the studio after completing the questionnaire, Klara entered Capaldi's office. To her surprise, she saw something that looked like Josie suspended in the air-it was an AF replica of Josie's body! As it turned out, Mr. Capaldi was not a painter but a scientist, who planned with Chrissie to transfer Klara's consciousness to the replica and make a new Josie if the real Josie were to die.
Capaldi: Klara, tell me what you think about the replica.
Klara: It resembles Josie quite accurately. Mr. Capaldi, you have done a good job of capturing Josie's appearance. I now understand why Chrissie asked me, at every step, to observe and learn Josie. The survey seems to test how well I have come to know Josie and how well I understand her decisions and feelings.
Capaldi: We will ask you to become her and to live in that replica of Josie with everything you have learned. Learn Josie, not just superficially, but deeply, entirely. You have to continue her for Chrissie and for everyone else who loves Josie.
Chrissie: I have doubts. I'm still not sure if this whole plan is the best thing we can do. I have been afraid of losing Josie ever since I lost Sal. That is why I agreed with you on this replica, but however well you make it, I don't think I will be able to accept this AF as my Josie.
Capaldi: You must not lose faith, Chrissie. The survey Klara has successfully completed is clear evidence that she is already well on her way to understanding all of Josie's drives and desires. You believe that there is something unreachable inside each of us, something that is unique and won't transfer. But there is nothing like that. The new Josie won't be an imitation. She will be the exact same person and you will have every right to love her just as you love Josie now.
Chrissie: But will I believe in it? When the day comes, will I really?
Klara: Excuse me, but I would like to say there is a chance you will never need the new Josie. She may overcome her illness. If the day comes when you do need the new Josie, I will do my best to become as close to her as possible. However, it is wrong to give up hope already.
(B) Capaldi believes that a person's identity can be fully understood and replicated through data, observations, and learned behavior. He represents a scientific, logical view that human essence can be measured. Chrissie, however, worries that some part of Josie is unique and cannot be copied. She represents an emotional and humanistic perspective that values feelings and inner essence. Their conversation highlights the tension between scientific replication and the irreplaceable qualities of being human.
